intro: You're looking for a business accountant near you, someone who can take the strain of year-end accounts, tax returns, VAT and payroll off your desk. Whether you're newly self-employed, running a growing limited company or simply want a local professional to talk things through with, the right accountant can make a real difference. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK accountant who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a business accountant near me usually need
need_lead: Most people who search for a business accountant near me want practical help with the financial side of running their business, from compliance to planning ahead.
needs: You've just started trading and need to understand what records to keep, when to register with HMRC and how to file your first tax return.
Your business has grown and you want someone local to prepare your year-end accounts and deal with Companies House filings on your behalf.
You're spending too much time on VAT returns and payroll and want a nearby accountant to take over the routine work so you can focus on the business.
You want management accounts or advice on tax planning to help you make decisions about pricing, hiring or investing.
You've had a letter from HMRC or a query about your tax position and want a professional nearby to look at it with you.
context_heading: What to understand about finding a business accountant near you
context: In the UK, the word "accountant" on its own is not a protected title, so anyone can call themselves an accountant. However, titles such as Chartered Accountant (ICAEW, ICAS or Chartered Accountants Ireland), Chartered Certified Accountant (ACCA) and Chartered Management Accountant (CIMA) are protected, and members are bound by their body's ethics, training and complaints rules. Only registered auditors can sign statutory audit reports.

Every practice offering accountancy services must also be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by a professional body or by HMRC. It is reasonable to ask which body supervises a firm, whether they hold professional indemnity insurance, and how complaints are handled. When you search for a business accountant near me, you're likely looking for someone you can meet or speak to easily, so location and accessibility matter.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Tell us what type of business you run, for example sole trader, partnership or limited company, and what industry you're in.
Let us know which services you need help with, such as year-end accounts, tax returns, VAT, payroll or management accounts.
Mention whether you already have an accountant or are starting fresh, and whether you need help with bookkeeping software.
Tell us your preferred way of working, whether you'd like to meet in person locally, work remotely, or a mix of both.
Let us know if you have any urgent deadlines or HMRC correspondence that needs attention.
Share your approximate turnover and number of employees so the accountant can understand the scale of your business.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the business accountant
questions: Which professional body are you a member of, and what title do you hold?
Who supervises your practice for anti-money-laundering purposes?
Do you hold professional indemnity insurance, and how are complaints handled?
What experience do you have with businesses in my sector?
How often will we be in contact, and will I have a named person to speak to?
Which accounting software do you recommend, and can you help with integrating it with my bank and invoicing?

faqs.q: Do I need a local accountant, or can I work with one further away?
faqs.a: Many businesses work with accountants remotely, but a local accountant can be helpful if you prefer face-to-face meetings or need to drop off records. It's a personal choice, and iComply can introduce you to a suitable professional based on your preferences.

faqs.q: What should I have ready before I speak to an accountant?
faqs.a: It helps to have your business structure, recent financial records, and any HMRC correspondence to hand. The accountant will then be able to give you a clearer picture of what they can do for you.

faqs.q: How do accountants charge for business services?
faqs.a: Accountants typically quote based on the work involved, such as the number of transactions, whether you need payroll or VAT returns, and the complexity of your affairs. Fees are usually agreed in advance, and iComply introduces you to an accountant who will quote you directly.

faqs.q: Can an accountant help if I'm behind on my tax returns?
faqs.a: Yes, accountants can help you get up to date and deal with HMRC on your behalf. It's best to be upfront about any overdue returns so they can advise you properly.
